player.name: Wren Ashdown
player.concept: a quick-witted half-elf ranger with a longbow, a dry sense of humour and a soft spot for underdogs

established: Gubbin let the courier go on his own terms and is still King Under the Mill.
canon: Corroded iron mill fittings lie by the walkway: brackets, a cracked gear with blunt teeth, and rust-dark bolts; none is crown-shaped.
Snikkit has offered to hand Hester over if Wren brings him Gubbin's pot-crown and makes Gubbin dead, gone, or laughed off his throne.
Gubbin briefly mistook Wren's cracked iron gear for a replacement crown, then became embarrassed when the goblins giggled.
Snikkit cut one strand of Hester’s hoist rope; she remains suspended, but the rope is weakened.
Gubbin knocked the cracked iron gear from Wren’s hand, and the watching goblins laughed at his angry reaction.
The goblins rejected Wren’s invented mill prophecy as a lie.
notes: Let the laughter sting Gubbin without making the coup complete: he still wears the crown and has the guards. Keep the newly weakened rope visible as pressure; Gubbin’s demand for an offer is a chance to bargain, use Hester’s notary role, or seize another opening.

transition.when: Wren proposes that Hester write a technically true, sealed document which Gubbin can interpret as recognition of his kingship, and tries to pass it off as the king-paper he demanded.

check.reason: to make Gubbin accept the true document as his king-paper
check.success: Gubbin accepts the paper as recognition and orders Hester lowered and handed over.
check.failure: Gubbin catches the trick or refuses to accept the paper as his king-paper; Hester remains on the rope.

patches.why: Hester can write a true document and Gubbin cannot read; this pays off the player's earlier focus on paperwork while leaving the deception uncertain.

repairs.assessment: Wren is enjoying a playful, inventive negotiation and has turned the search for a crown into a live political opening. Snikkit has made his bargain; the scene is on track and ready for Wren to accept, refuse, or reshape it.

Wren is enjoying a comic, high-risk con and has brought the crown succession into public view. Gubbin is awake and embarrassed, but still in command; the scene is on track at the moment where Wren can press the joke or change tactics.
repairs.notes: Let Gubbin's demand for his king-paper or defense of the pot give Wren a chance to embarrass him further, rather than resolving the coup automatically. Snikkit can exploit any opening, but keep his knife on the rope and Hester's danger present.

repairs.assessment: Wren is enjoying bold, theatrical bluffs and has made Gubbin look ridiculous, but the failed prophecy has sharpened the danger. The scene is still moving: Gubbin wants an offer, and Hester is at immediate risk.
repairs.notes: Let the laughter sting Gubbin without making the coup complete: he still wears the crown and has the guards. Keep the newly weakened rope visible as pressure; Gubbin’s demand for an offer is a chance to bargain, use Hester’s notary role, or seize another opening.

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
The burnt mill creaks around you. Through a gap in the floor, the black mill-race roars beneath the undercroft, its water flashing dimly in the tallowlight along two narrow walkways. Six goblins lean on spears and grumble. Above the channel, a narrow goblin straddles the hoist beam, a knife laid across the rope; below him, a woman hangs in a grain sack over the rushing water.

“—and no seal, however grandly demanded, makes a false instrument lawful,” she says, turning slowly. “Your chief may have his king-paper when he finds a king willing to sign it.”

“By moonrise, paper-lady,” the goblin purrs. “Or down you go. Humble Snikkit advises you to reconsider.”

At the far end, something large snores behind a moth-eaten curtain. Nobody below has looked up yet. What do you do?

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I lean over the gap in the floorboards, tip my hat, and call down in my brightest shop-counter voice. "Evening, gents! And madam. Wren Ashdown, Ashdown and Associates, Risk Management. Couldn't help overhearing you've got a hostage dangling over a mill-race on a single rope. Bold. Very bold. Now, has anybody down there given any thought to insurance?"

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Your voice carries cleanly down through the broken floor—and the mill-race swallows the echo.

Snikkit’s knife lifts from the rope. He twists on the beam, both long ears pricked toward the gap. The goblins below stop grumbling and look up; one raises a sling, uncertain. The courier’s slow turning brings her face toward you.

“Insurance?” Snikkit says, tasting the word. “Your humble Snikkit appreciates a mutual arrangement. You come down, tall friend. We discuss the important bits.”

From behind the curtain, a huge goblin snores on, unmoved.

The woman in the sack fixes you with a sharp look. “Wren Ashdown, if you’re offering coverage, I suggest you begin with the rope.”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I climb down through the gap, slow and friendly, hands where everyone can see them, and produce a scrap of paper and a stub of charcoal from my coat. I start writing as I talk. "Right. Standard Hostage Retention Policy. Here's your exposure, Mister Snikkit: your asset is only worth anything while she's alive and dry. One slip of that knife, and your asset's gone, your leverage is gone, and your chief's king-paper floats off to the sea. Terrible position. Uninsurable, frankly. BUT. Our policy requires a second rope, a safety rider, tied off at the walkway. And a modest premium." I tap the charcoal toward his blade. "Shall we say... the knife?"

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
You ease down the rotten ladder, hands open. The goblins track every step with their spears, but none thrusts. At the bottom, the race’s spray dampens your paper; Snikkit watches your charcoal with keen suspicion.

At “the knife,” he curls his fingers around the handle. “A premium is paid by the customer, tall friend. Your policy protects the paper-lady. Gubbin’s policy protects the warren.”

He leans closer, voice pitched just for you. “King-paper. Big seal. Says Gubbin is king. By moonrise. Then perhaps the knife can retire.”

Hester gives a brittle laugh from the sack. “Do not put my seal to that.”

Snikkit glances between your paper and her satchel. “So, Wren Ashdown. What have you brought that is worth more than a knife?”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I fold the policy away with a sigh, as if he's just turned down the bargain of the century. "Mister Snikkit, a seal is just wax. Any clerk with a candle can make one. Paper doesn't make a king. You know what makes a king? A CROWN. And a coronation. And a prophecy, ideally. The paper-lady can't give you any of those." I lower my voice to match his. "I can. Royal coronation consultant, twelve years' experience, very discreet." While I talk I'm scanning the undercroft for anything round, metal and vaguely regal. A mill this old must have its gear wheels lying about somewhere.

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Snikkit’s eyes brighten at “coronation consultant.” He glances toward the distant throne, then back at you. “A crown, yes. A very important-looking thing. Our humble Snikkit has been thinking—perhaps a new king would appreciate professional advice.”

There are old iron mill fittings scattered by the walkway, but nothing crown-shaped: just corroded brackets, a cracked gear with blunt teeth, and rust-dark bolts.

Snikkit leans close, voice soft as a secret. “Gubbin’s pot-crown. Bring it to me, and make him finished—dead, gone, or laughed out of his throne. Then the paper-lady is yours. No charge.”

Hester twists in the sack. “That is an appalling arrangement,” she says loudly. Then, quieter: “Could it work?”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I stick out a hand to shake on it. "Mister Snikkit, you've just hired the finest regime-change consultant north of the crossroads. But nothing is ever no charge. Standard terms: the client's collateral comes off the beam and onto the walkway, tied up as tight as you like, as a gesture of good faith. Damp collateral depreciates." Then, as if it's the most natural thing in the world, I stoop and pick up the cracked gear with the blunt teeth, knock the rust off on my boot, and turn it over in the tallowlight with a connoisseur's squint. "Hm. Yes. This'll do nicely."

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
The cracked gear is all iron teeth and rust—heavy, blunt, and not remotely a crown. Still, it catches the tallowlight when you turn it in your hands.

Snikkit’s ears tilt forward. “A fine symbol of office,” he murmurs. “When you bring the real crown, I will make a most generous client.”

Hester swings a few inches over the race. “Loudly: I object to being used as collateral in a coup. Quietly: are you actually going to depose him, Wren?”

Snikkit’s knife stays on the rope. “You have a plan, consultant?”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: "A plan? Mister Snikkit, I have a five-phase strategic roadmap." I count on my fingers. "Phase one: due diligence. Phase two: asset substitution. Phase three: reputational restructuring. Phases four and five are confidential." I wink up at Hester. "Madam, hang in there. Professionally speaking." Then I tuck the gear behind my back and tiptoe along the walkway toward the moth-eaten curtain, stepping over anything that looks like it might creak, and ease one corner of it aside to get a look at the sleeping chief and his famous pot-crown.

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
You tuck the cracked gear behind your back and creep along the wall-side walkway. The mill-race roars beside you; underfoot, the old planks flex but hold.

At the curtain’s edge, you ease it aside. Two enormous goblins doze near a throne piled from grain sacks. Beyond them, Gubbin sleeps round as one, a dented copper pot jammed over his brow, a gnawed bone across his belly. The pot-crown is real—and the guards are close enough that taking it would be no quiet trick.

Behind you, Snikkit whispers, “Due diligence. Very wise.”

Hester turns slowly above the water. “Loudly: This is a grotesque proposal. Quietly: If you can get that pot, perhaps.” The guards’ breathing rumbles in the dim. What do you do?

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: Quiet was never my strong suit. I straighten my coat, sweep the curtain fully aside, and rap my knuckles smartly on the side of the copper pot. CLONK. "Wakey wakey, your majesty! Crown Inspectorate, annual headwear audit." I flash the damp policy paper at the guards as if it's a warrant. "I'm afraid this crown has failed on several counts. It has a HANDLE, sir. A king with a handle can be picked up and carried off by anybody. Shocking oversight. I'll have to confiscate it for testing." I hold out the gear with great ceremony. "Here's your regulation temporary replacement."

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
The copper pot answers your knuckles with a ringing CLONK. Gubbin bolts upright, the pot tilting over one eye. Lump and Other Lump lumber to their feet behind him.

“Crown Inspectorate?” Gubbin bellows. He snatches the damp paper, squints at it, then spots the iron gear. His mouth falls open. “A spare crown! For us?”

A few goblins giggle. Gubbin’s delight curdles. “Handle is for holding! We is king, and we keeps our crown.” He lurches toward you, bone sceptre raised. “Where is our king-paper? And why is the warren laughing?” Snikkit stays by the rope, knife poised. The watching goblins lean in.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I don't flinch from the sceptre. I raise one finger, like a clerk who has heard it all before. "Your majesty, they're laughing because word's got round your paperwork isn't in order. Happens to every new king. But I can fix it, and I can fix it by moonrise." I nod at Hester dangling over the race. "Regulation fourteen-b: a king-paper is only valid if the notary signs and seals it on dry ground, with both hands free, witnessed by a certified inspector. That's me. Nobody has ever signed a lawful instrument from inside a sack. Ask her." I turn to the guards. "Lump, Other Lump, if you'd be so good as to fetch the notary down to the walkway? The king is waiting."

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Gubbin’s raised sceptre falters. The watching goblins go very still at your mention of a notary—and then a few snickers escape.

“Dry ground?” he rumbles. “Both hands?” He looks at Hester hanging over the race, then at the gear in your hand. “We is not signing from a sack!”

Lump and Other Lump glance to Gubbin, waiting for an order. Before he can give one, Snikkit calls from the beam, “A proper king gets his paperwork in order!” His knife remains against the rope.

Hester turns toward Gubbin. “I can write a true document on dry ground. I will not certify you king.”

Gubbin’s face reddens beneath the tilted pot. “Then bring the notary down! And you, Inspector—prove that iron thing is fit for a king!” The goblins watch, their laughter hovering.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I hold the gear aloft so the tallowlight catches every rusty tooth, and drop my voice into a deep, sonorous register. "Fit for a king? Your majesty, this is no iron thing. This is THE WHEEL. It turned this river for forty years. And every mill-child north of the crossroads knows the old prophecy." I close my eyes and recite. "When the mill is burnt and the wheel is still, a king shall rise from beneath the hill. Crown him with iron, not with copper or tin, and the warren shall bow and his reign begin. But the crown must be set on the royal head... by the hand of one who hung by a thread." I open my eyes and point solemnly up at Hester. "Very specific prophecy. Very old. Can't argue with it."

transcript.speaker: dice
transcript.text: Deception check to fool a goblin into believing your lie: 1 + 2 = 3 vs DC 13: failure (natural 1!)

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
For one breath, the warren is silent.

Then Lump snorts. “Mill-children know no prophecy.”

Gubbin’s face darkens. “We is king already! No prophecy needed!” He sweeps the iron gear from your hand with his sceptre. It clatters across the stones, and the watching goblins burst into laughter—not at your tale now, but at the furious king trying to look grand beneath his dented pot.

Snikkit’s knife scrapes across the rope. A fresh strand parts. Hester jerks in the sack, turning above the black water.

“Enough stories, tall friend,” Snikkit says, suddenly cold. “Your words are worth nothing here. Gubbin wants his paper. What do you offer him?”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I watch the strand part and my smile doesn't move an inch, though my voice speeds up considerably. "Fair. Prophecy was a stretch. Let's talk paper." I flip the damp policy over, grab the nearest tallow candle, and write in big charcoal capitals: GUBBIN IS KING. SIGNED, THE KING. "Your majesty, think it through. Who can make a king? Only a king. A notary's seal just says some clerk reckons you're king. But YOUR seal says the king himself says so. Who's going to argue with the king?" I drip a fat puddle of tallow onto the bottom of the paper and hold it up to him. "Press your crown into that. Best seal in the land. Then you don't need her seal at all, and the notary can come down off that rope."

transcript.speaker: dice
transcript.text: Persuasion check to persuade Gubbin to accept a different price: 15 + 2 = 17 vs DC 13: success

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Gubbin stares at the paper, then at the tallow puddle. The anger in his face eases into delighted consideration.

“King signs for king,” he rumbles. “That is very official.”

He presses the copper rim of his pot into the warm tallow. A lopsided ring of wax clings to the page. The goblins gasp at the seal; Gubbin lifts it high, reclaimed dignity swelling his chest. “Behold! Gubbin is king, by the king’s own hand!”

Snikkit keeps his knife poised, but Gubbin jabs his bone sceptre toward him. “Lower the paper-lady. The king has made a bargain.”

Snikkit pays out the rope. Hester reaches the walkway, shaken but alive, and pulls the sack down from her shoulders. “A legally imaginative transaction,” she says, steadying herself. “Wren, I owe you a debt.”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I offer Hester my arm and steer her gently toward the ladder. "A debt? Lovely. Ashdown and Associates accepts coin, promissory notes, and glowing references. I'll send an invoice." Then, because I simply cannot help myself, I turn back to Gubbin with a polite little cough. "Oh, and your majesty, one small formality. You'll find on the reverse of your king-paper the Standard Hostage Retention Policy, which you have now sealed with your own crown. Very binding, as you said yourself. The premium is due on signing." I hold out my palm. "I'll take it in silver, or in that bone, if it's a good bone."

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Hester accepts your arm, but before you can steer her anywhere, Gubbin clutches the sealed paper to his chest.

“Premium?” he bellows. “The king has paid with a king-paper! You may go, before we charge you for standing in our hall.”

Snikkit lowers the rope the last few feet, watching Gubbin rather than you. The cut strand still hangs loose. Hester steps onto the walkway, pale and damp, then checks that her satchel is fastened and dry.

“The goblins were waiting at the ford,” she says crisply. “They went straight for my satchel. This was no chance raid.” She looks toward the ladder. “I must reach the Saltmere delegation in Caerwyn before the Assembly opens. And I would rather not walk the King’s Road barefoot and alone.”

Behind you, Gubbin waves his paper like a banner. “The king’s court is dismissed!”
